Baghdad-Iraq.name: Baghdad
Baghdad-Iraq.evidence_basis: East and West Bank Abbasid metropolis (~1,400 ha active late Abbasid fabric; Lassner 1970; Adams 1965) revived under Caliph al-Nasir before Hulagu's 1258 sack (~70-75% drop), partial Ilkhanid-Jalayirid recovery (Mustawfi 1340), 1348 plague and Timur's 1401 massacre.

Tabriz-Iran.name: Tabriz
Tabriz-Iran.evidence_basis: Spared 1221 Mongol sack by tribute; exploded into the Ilkhanate's premier metropolis under Ghazan Khan (25 km Ghazaniyya wall circuit and Rab-i Rashidi suburb; Mustawfi 1340; Marco Polo; Melville); hit by 1348 plague, reviving as Qara and Aq Qoyunlu imperial capital.

Herat-Afghanistan.name: Herat
Herat-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Square walled core (~200 ha) plus vast Hari Rud oasis suburbs flourished under Seljuks and Ghurids before Tolui/Eljigidei's 1221-22 Mongol destruction; rebuilt by Kartids (Saifi Harawi) and surged to ~140k-155k as Timurid imperial capital under Shah Rukh and Husayn Bayqara (Subtelny 2007; Allen 1983).

Nishapur-Iran.name: Nishapur
Nishapur-Iran.evidence_basis: Pre-Mongol Khorasan metropolis (~1,200 ha survey footprint; Bulliet 1972; Wilkinson 1973) shattered by 1145 earthquake and 1153 Ghuzz sack, rebuilt at Shadyakh, then devastated by Tolui's 1221 Mongol sack and 1280 earthquake (Melville 1980).

Ghazni-Afghanistan.name: Ghazni
Ghazni-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Imperial capital of the Ghaznavid Empire (80 ha citadel/walled core plus sprawling palatial rabads; Bombaci; Inaba 2013); burned by Ghurid Ala al-Din Jahansuz in 1151 and devastated by Mongols in 1221, shrinking to a modest provincial town (Ibn Battuta; Baburnama).

Isfahan-Iran.name: Isfahan
Isfahan-Iran.evidence_basis: Great Seljuk imperial capital (~15 km wall circuit reported by Nasir-i Khusraw; Durand-Guedy 2010, 2020) weakened by 12th-c. Shafi'i-Hanafi strife and 1237 Mongol takeover, revived under Ilkhanids/Muzaffarids, then devastated by Timur's 1387 massacre.

Damascus-Syria.name: Damascus
Damascus-Syria.evidence_basis: Walled core (~105 ha) plus vast Ghuta/Salihiyya/Midan suburbs grew under Zengid, Ayyubid and Bahri Mamluk rule (Ashtor; Lapidus; Chamberlain 1994); lost ~35% in 1348 Black Death (Dols) and suffered Timur's 1401 sack and artisan deportation.

Rayy-Iran.name: Rayy
Rayy-Iran.evidence_basis: Major Seljuk imperial metropolis (~500 ha archaeological footprint; Rante & Afround 2015) already strained by Hanafi-Shafi'i-Shi'i sectarian wars before Jebe and Subutai's 1220 sack permanently shifted urban life to Varamin and Tehran.

Mosul-Iraq.name: Mosul
Mosul-Iraq.evidence_basis: Walled Tigris metropolis (~290 ha) reaching its medieval zenith under the Zengids and Badr al-Din Lu'lu' (1234-59) in metalwork and muslin trade (Patton 1991; Ibn Jubayr); severely devastated by the 1262 Mongol sack and 1393 Timurid raid.

Balkh-Afghanistan.name: Balkh
Balkh-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Massive walled oasis metropolis (>120 ha Bala Hissar plus extensive outer ramparts; Le Berre & Schlumberger) devastated by Genghis Khan in 1221 (Juvaini); still largely ruined when Ibn Battuta visited in 1333, reviving under 15th-c. Timurid canal restoration (Subtelny; McChesney).

Shiraz-Iran.name: Shiraz
Shiraz-Iran.evidence_basis: Capital of Fars spared Mongol destruction by Salghurid submission; flourished continuously under Injuids, Muzaffarids, Timurids and Aq Qoyunlu as a major garden, wine, silk and literary metropolis (Mustawfi 1340; Limbert 2004; Ibn Battuta).

Aleppo-Syria.name: Aleppo
Aleppo-Syria.evidence_basis: Inner walled city (~160 ha) plus dense northern/eastern rabads flourished under Zengids and Ayyubids (Sauvaget 1941; Tabbaa 1997); suffered severe contractions from Hulagu's 1260 sack, 1348 Black Death and Timur's 1400 sack before late Mamluk spice-trade recovery.

Konya-Turkey.name: Konya
Konya-Turkey.evidence_basis: Capital of the Rum Seljuks; Ala al-Din Kayqubad's 1221 wall circuit (~4.5 km) plus sprawling rabads described by Ibn Bibi, Aflaki, Cahen (Pre-Ottoman Turkey) and Peacock (2021) indicate an ~85k 13th-c. zenith before post-Ilkhanid contraction, 1348 Black Death and Karamanid-Ottoman stabilization.

Ani-Turkey.name: Ani
Ani-Turkey.evidence_basis: Double-walled Bagratid Armenian metropolis (~100 ha intra-mural plus extensive canyon suburbs; Hewsen 2001; Eastmond) flourishing again under Shaddadids and Georgian Zakarians until the 1236 Mongol sack, 1319 earthquake and shift of Silk Road trade.

Sultaniyya-Iran.name: Sultaniyya
Sultaniyya-Iran.evidence_basis: Planned imperial capital founded in 1304 by Ilkhan Oljeitu (790 ha monumental zone; Mustawfi ranked it second only to Tabriz in 1340); contracted rapidly after Ilkhanid fragmentation, Black Death and 1384/1405 Timurid campaigns (Blair 1986; Haneda 1997).

Tbilisi-Georgia.name: Tbilisi
Tbilisi-Georgia.evidence_basis: Jafarid emirate taken by David IV in 1122 to become the cosmopolitan capital of the Georgian Golden Age under Queen Tamar (~75-80k; Rayfield 2012; Kartlis Tskhovreba); devastated by Jalal al-Din Khwarazmshah (1226), Black Death and Timur's eight campaigns (1386-1403).

Sivas-Turkey.name: Sivas
Sivas-Turkey.evidence_basis: Major Seljuk and Eretnid commercial hub with Genoese consulate and extensive waqf complexes noted by Ibn Battuta and William of Rubruck; contracted in 1348 plague and devastated by Timur's 1400 siege and garrison massacre (Cahen; Peacock 2021).

Bursa-Turkey.name: Bursa
Bursa-Turkey.evidence_basis: Byzantine walled town conquered by Orhan in 1326 as first Ottoman imperial capital; rapid silk-trade and kulliye expansion attested by Ibn Battuta, Bertrandon de la Broquiere and the 1487 Ottoman tahrir defter (>6,400 taxpaying households plus exempt military/suburban groups; Inalcik; Faroqhi).

Hamadan-Iran.name: Hamadan
Hamadan-Iran.evidence_basis: Summer capital of the Iraqi Seljuks in the 12th century (Alaviyan Dome); stormed and heavily depopulated by Mongols in 1221 (Juvaini; Ibn al-Athir), recovering as a mid-tier Zagros hub (Mustawfi 1340).

Yazd-Iran.name: Yazd
Yazd-Iran.evidence_basis: Qanat-irrigated oasis spared Mongol devastation; expanded steadily under Kakuyids, Atabegs, Muzaffarids and Timurids (Jami Mosque, Amir Chakhmaq) as Iran's premier silk-brocade weaving hub (Marco Polo; Mustawfi; Ja'fari Tarikh-i Yazd).

Antioch-Turkey.name: Antioch
Antioch-Turkey.evidence_basis: Byzantine regional capital and seat of the Crusader Principality of Antioch (multi-ethnic Greek, Syriac, Armenian and Frankish populace within ~350 ha ancient circuit, largely settled in lower plain; Cahen 1940) until catastrophic 1268 Mamluk destruction by Baybars.

Ganja-Azerbaijan.name: Ganja
Ganja-Azerbaijan.evidence_basis: Shaddadid and Ildegizid metropolis of Arran (home of Nizami Ganjavi); suffered the catastrophic 1139 earthquake (rebuilt 4 km north), 1225 Khwarazmian occupation and 1235 Mongol siege (Kirakos Gandzaketsi; Wordsworth 2018; Campbell 2021).

Maragha-Iran.name: Maragha
Maragha-Iran.evidence_basis: Ahmadili Atabeg seat sacked by Jebe and Subutai in 1221; boomed as Hulagu's first Ilkhanid capital (1256-65) and Nasir al-Din al-Tusi's observatory before yielding primacy to Tabriz (Mustawfi 1340; Lane 2003).

Basra-Iraq.name: Basra
Basra-Iraq.evidence_basis: Early Islamic misr contracted from its western desert site (al-Zubayr) toward the Shatt al-Arab canals; Ibn Battuta (1327) and Mustawfi (1340) describe ruined outer quarters surrounding a still-active Gulf date and spice port (Adams; Ashtor).

Hormuz-Iran.name: Hormuz
Hormuz-Iran.evidence_basis: Relocated in 1300 from mainland Minab to Jarun Island to escape Chagatai raids; became the premier Indian Ocean-Persian Gulf entrepot (horse, pearl and spice trade) praised as extraordinarily populous by Ibn Battuta, Abd al-Razzaq (1442) and Portuguese accounts (Floor 2006).

Mashhad-Iran.name: Mashhad
Mashhad-Iran.evidence_basis: Pilgrimage town around Imam Reza's tomb (Sanabad) noted as thriving by Ibn Battuta (1333); superseded ruined Tus after 1389 and boomed under Timurid Shah Rukh and Gawhar Shad's 1418 mosque and waqf complex (Subtelny).

Kayseri-Turkey.name: Kayseri
Kayseri-Turkey.evidence_basis: Seljuk secondary capital and Yabanlu international fair nexus; suffered 1243 Mongol sack after Kosedag (Ibn Bibi) and 1348 plague, rebounding under Eretnid, Qadi Burhan al-Din and early Ottoman administration (Cahen; Faroqhi; Peacock 2021).

Mecca-Saudi Arabia.name: Mecca
Mecca-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Hashemite Sharifate sanctuary city sustained by Egyptian/Syrian grain waqfs and annual Hajj commerce (Ibn Jubayr 1183; Ibn Battuta 1326; Mortel 1987); late 15th-c. growth tied to Jeddah's Mamluk spice-trade surge.

Acre-Israel.name: Acre
Acre-Israel.evidence_basis: Peninsular walled city plus Montmusard suburb (~90 ha combined) expanded after 1191 as capital of the Latin Kingdom of Jerusalem with Venetian, Genoese and Pisan communes (Jacoby; Prawer; Ellenblum) until razed by Mamluk Sultan al-Ashraf Khalil in 1291.

Aden-Yemen.name: Aden
Aden-Yemen.evidence_basis: Premier Red Sea-Indian Ocean entrepot of the Karimi spice trade documented by Cairo Geniza letters, Rasulid customs registers (Nur al-Maarif) and Zheng He's fleets (Margariti 2007; Vallet 2010), easing slightly after Jeddah's 15th-c. Mamluk diversion.

Trebizond-Turkey.name: Trebizond
Trebizond-Turkey.evidence_basis: Capital of the Grand Komnenoi (1204-1461) and primary Black Sea outlet for Ilkhanid Tabriz caravan trade with Genoese/Venetian quarters; hit by 1347-48 plague and post-1461 Ottoman deportations reflected in 1486 tahrir defter (Bryer; Lowry 1981).

Diyarbakir-Turkey.name: Diyarbakir
Diyarbakir-Turkey.evidence_basis: Massive 5.5 km basalt wall circuit (~145 ha) prospered under Marwanids, Artuqids and as the 15th-c. Aq Qoyunlu capital under Uzun Hasan before 1518 Ottoman tahrir records (~50k; Gabriel 1940; Woods 1999).

Tus-Iran.name: Tus
Tus-Iran.evidence_basis: Walled Tabaran-Tus city (~400 ha) suffered 1220 Mongol sack, revived partially under Ilkhanid governor Arghun Aqa (Radkan pastures; Melville), then permanently ruined by Timurid prince Miran Shah in 1389 as residents moved to Mashhad.

Zaranj-Afghanistan.name: Zaranj
Zaranj-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Nasrid and Mihrabanid capital of Sistan (Tarikh-i Sistan; Fischer survey) sustained by Helmand dams; damaged by Mongols (1222) and permanently devastated when Timur destroyed the Band-i Rustam dam and city in 1383.

Zabid-Yemen.name: Zabid
Zabid-Yemen.evidence_basis: Circular walled Tihama metropolis (~135 ha; Ciuk & Keall) serving as Najahid, Ayyubid and Rasulid winter capital and Sunni madrasa university center (over 60 documented madrasas; Vallet 2010; Ibn Battuta).

Sanaa-Yemen.name: Sanaa
Sanaa-Yemen.evidence_basis: Walled northern highland metropolis (~150 ha old city; Serjeant & Lewcock 1983) serving as Sulayhid capital, contested Rasulid-Zaydi prize and chief interior textile and craft center.

Shamakhi-Azerbaijan.name: Shamakhi
Shamakhi-Azerbaijan.evidence_basis: Long-standing capital of the Shirvanshahs and major Caspian raw-silk emporium (Minorsky 1958); struck by the 1192 earthquake and 1222 Mongol raid but prospered in the 15th c. under Ibrahim I and Khalilullah I (Contarini).

Kerman-Iran.name: Kerman
Kerman-Iran.evidence_basis: Capital of the Seljuks of Kerman (1041-1186), Qutlughkhanids and Muzaffarids; avoided full Mongol devastation via Baraq Hajib's submission, sustained by Hormuz-Khorasan caravan trade and wool/shawl crafts (Mustawfi; Marco Polo).

Firuzkuh-Afghanistan.name: Firuzkuh
Firuzkuh-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Summer imperial capital of the Shansabani Ghurids founded c. 1146 along the Hari Rud gorge (Minaret of Jam 1194, Jewish cemetery, terraced slopes; Thomas 2018; Juzjani); systematically destroyed by Ogedei's Mongol army in 1222 and soon deserted.

Erzurum-Turkey.name: Erzurum
Erzurum-Turkey.evidence_basis: Swelled after 1049 Seljuk sack of nearby Artze; Saltuqid and Rum Seljuk trade emporium on the Tabriz-Trebizond road, severely sacked by Baiju's Mongols in 1242 and later contested by Qara and Aq Qoyunlu (Cahen; Peacock).

Ardabil-Iran.name: Ardabil
Ardabil-Iran.evidence_basis: Historic Azerbaijan commercial city raided by Georgians (1209; Guven 2024) and sacked by Mongols (1220; Ibn al-Athir); revived strongly from c. 1300 around Shaykh Safi al-Din's Safaviyya Sufi shrine and waqf estate (Mustawfi; Morton).

Qazvin-Iran.name: Qazvin
Qazvin-Iran.evidence_basis: Walled Jibal fortress and hometown of Hamdallah Mustawfi (Nuzhat al-Qulub 1340 gives detailed ward and tax revenue figures); suffered 1220 Mongol massacre (Ibn al-Athir) but revived near Ilkhanid Sultaniyya.

Hillah-Iraq.name: Hillah
Hillah-Iraq.evidence_basis: Founded in 1101 by Mazyadid Amir Sadaqa ibn Mansur on the Euphrates; spared destruction in 1258 by submitting peacefully to Hulagu, thriving as Iraq's foremost Twelver Shi'i seminary town (Ibn Battuta; Mustawfi).

Ahlat-Turkey.name: Ahlat
Ahlat-Turkey.evidence_basis: Capital of the Shah-Armen dynasty (1100-1207) and Ayyubid bastion attested by its vast Seljuk-period cemetery (over 8,000 monumental tombstones); devastated by Jalal al-Din's 1230 siege, 1246 earthquake and Mongol rule (Peacock; Sinclair).

Kashan-Iran.name: Kashan
Kashan-Iran.evidence_basis: Leading medieval center of fritware lustre pottery, glazed tiles and silk velvets (Watson 1985; Mustawfi 1340); partially sacked in 1224 but quickly recovered under Ilkhanid, Timurid and Aq Qoyunlu patronage.

Kandahar-Afghanistan.name: Kandahar
Kandahar-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Excavations at Shahr-i Kohna (McNicoll & Ball 1996; Crowe 1996) document active Ghaznavid, Ghurid, Ilkhanid and Timurid-Arghun occupation along the main Herat-Multan commercial corridor.

Tokat-Turkey.name: Tokat
Tokat-Turkey.evidence_basis: Major Danishmendid and Seljuk fortress-emporium on the Tabriz-Bursa silk highway, spared Timur's 1400 destruction of Sivas and expanding rapidly in 15th-c. Ottoman tahrir records (Faroqhi; Cahen).

Amasya-Turkey.name: Amasya
Amasya-Turkey.evidence_basis: Yesilirmak gorge citadel town under Danishmendids, Seljuks and Ilkhanids (1308 bimaristan), flourishing in the 15th century as Ottoman crown-prince (sehzade) administrative capital (Cahen; Faroqhi).

Tripoli-Lebanon.name: Tripoli
Tripoli-Lebanon.evidence_basis: Banu Ammar silk/paper metropolis and Crusader County capital (El-Mina peninsula) until razed by Qalawun in 1289 and rebuilt inland around Mons Peregrinus as a thriving Mamluk provincial capital (Salam-Liebich 1983; Ashtor).

Iznik-Turkey.name: Iznik
Iznik-Turkey.evidence_basis: Late Roman 4.9 km walled enclosure (~150 ha) served as capital of the Empire of Nicaea (1204-1261); declined after Byzantine return to Constantinople and 1331 Ottoman siege (Ibn Battuta described extensive inner gardens; Foss 1996).

Sis-Turkey.name: Sis
Sis-Turkey.evidence_basis: Royal capital and Catholicosate seat of the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia from Levon I (1198), flourishing with Ayas transit trade until 1348 plague and 1375 Mamluk conquest and sack (Mutafian 2012; Boase).

Bamiyan-Afghanistan.name: Bamiyan
Bamiyan-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Capital of the Bamiyan branch of the Ghurids (1155-1215) controlling the Hindu Kush passes; completely razed and depopulated by Genghis Khan in 1221 after Mutugen's death (Juvaini; Baker & Allchin), remaining a small valley settlement thereafter.

Kabul-Afghanistan.name: Kabul
Kabul-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Strategic gateway to the Khyber and Hindu Kush passes; eclipsed by Ghazni in the 11th-12th centuries and noted as modest by Ibn Battuta (1333), before booming in the late 15th century as Timurid Ulugh Beg II's capital (Baburnama).

Erbil-Iraq.name: Erbil
Erbil-Iraq.evidence_basis: Citadel tell (~10 ha) plus extensive lower walled town boomed under Begteginid Emir Muzaffar al-Din Gokbori (1190-1233; Ibn Khallikan) before 1258-59 Mongol siege and 1310 massacre (Mustawfi).

Amol-Iran.name: Amol
Amol-Iran.evidence_basis: Principal medieval city of Tabaristan/Mazandaran on the Haraz River under Bavandids and Marashi Sayyids; hit by 1221 Mongol raid and Timur's brutal 1392 sack (Ibn Isfandiyar; Zahir al-Din Marashi; Melville).

Bust-Afghanistan.name: Bust
Bust-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Helmand-Arghandab confluence fortress and Ghaznavid winter palace complex (Lashkari Bazar excavations, Schlumberger & Sourdel-Thomine 1978); burned by Ghurids in 1151 and devastated by Mongols in 1221.

Ankara-Turkey.name: Ankara
Ankara-Turkey.evidence_basis: Walled hilltop citadel and lower commercial quarters governed by Seljuk notables and akhi fraternities (Wittek 1932; Peacock 2021), growing with late 15th-c. mohair-textile exports (Faroqhi).

Wasit-Iraq.name: Wasit
Wasit-Iraq.evidence_basis: Twin-bank Lower Tigris agricultural hub and Ilkhanid-Jalayirid mint (Safar 1945 excavations; Adams 1981); steadily contracted as the Tigris shifted eastward into the Amara channel in the late 15th century.

Nakhchivan-Azerbaijan.name: Nakhchivan
Nakhchivan-Azerbaijan.evidence_basis: Primary capital of the Ildegizid Atabegs (Momine Khatun mausoleum 1186); sacked by Jalal al-Din (1225) and Mongols before reviving as an Ilkhanid Aras-valley node (William of Rubruck; Mustawfi; Campbell 2021).

Al-Hasa-Saudi Arabia.name: Al-Hasa
Al-Hasa-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Massive spring-fed palm oasis and Qarmatian capital described as populous and walled by Nasir-i Khusraw (1051); remained eastern Arabia's largest urban seat under Uyunids, Usfurids and Jabrids (al-Juhany; Smith).

Taiz-Yemen.name: Taiz
Taiz-Yemen.evidence_basis: Fortified highland capital of the Ayyubids and Rasulids (1229-1454) below Jabal Sabir with Ashrafiyya and Muzaffariyya complexes and royal mint; praised as one of Yemen's finest cities by Ibn Battuta (Smith 1997; Vallet 2010).

Erzincan-Turkey.name: Erzincan
Erzincan-Turkey.evidence_basis: Prosperous Mengujekid and Eretnid-Mutahharten capital famed for silk and buckram textiles (Marco Polo; Ibn Battuta), repeatedly struck by severe earthquakes (1254, 1374, 1458) and Timurid-Ottoman wars (Cahen).

Edessa-Turkey.name: Edessa
Edessa-Turkey.evidence_basis: Byzantine and Crusader County capital (~100 ha walled area) until Imad al-Din Zengi's 1144 conquest and 1146 massacre of the Christian population (Segal 1970; Ibn al-Athir), later an Ayyubid, Mamluk and Aq Qoyunlu town.

Hama-Syria.name: Hama
Hama-Syria.evidence_basis: Autonomous Ayyubid principality under Abu al-Fida (1310-31) with famous Orontes norias and textile industry; hit by 1157 earthquake, 1348 plague and Timur's 1400 passage (Ashtor; Riis).

Medina-Saudi Arabia.name: Medina
Medina-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Walled sanctuary city and fertile date-palm oasis governed by Husaynid emirs under Ayyubid and Mamluk suzerainty with major royal waqf endowments and Hajj provisioning (al-Samhudi; Mortel).

Nicosia-Cyprus.name: Nicosia
Nicosia-Cyprus.evidence_basis: Byzantine provincial seat elevated in 1192 to royal capital of Lusignan Cyprus; expanded with Latin, Greek and Syrian quarters before losing ~35-40% in the 1348 Black Death and 1426 Mamluk sack (Edbury; Coureas; Machairas).

Kutahya-Turkey.name: Kutahya
Kutahya-Turkey.evidence_basis: Fortified Byzantine stronghold becoming capital of the Germiyanid Beylik (c. 1300) and then administrative capital of Ottoman Anadolu Beylerbeyligi in 1451 (Varlik 1974; Faroqhi).

Antalya-Turkey.name: Antalya
Antalya-Turkey.evidence_basis: Key Byzantine and Rum Seljuk Mediterranean emporium (taken 1207) linking Anatolia with Cyprus and Egypt; Ibn Battuta describes segregated walled Muslim, Greek, Jewish and Frankish quarters (Redford; Cahen).

Kutaisi-Georgia.name: Kutaisi
Kutaisi-Georgia.evidence_basis: Royal capital of unified Bagratid Georgia until 1122 (Bagrati Cathedral 1003, Gelati Academy 1106), remaining the seat of western Georgia/Kingdom of Imereti sheltered west of the Likhi range from full Mongol devastation (Rayfield 2012).

Qom-Iran.name: Qom
Qom-Iran.evidence_basis: Prominent Shi'i shrine city (Fatima Masumeh) heavily damaged by Mongols in 1224 (Mustawfi notes half-ruined quarters in 1340 despite eight Ilkhanid tomb towers; Campbell 2021), rebounding slowly in the 15th century.

Mardin-Turkey.name: Mardin
Mardin-Turkey.evidence_basis: Hilltop citadel and terraced stone town serving as capital of the Artuqids of Mardin (1108-1409) with major madrasas and wool/silk weaving praised by Ibn Battuta; weathered Timurid sieges (1394, 1401) and passed to Aq Qoyunlu (Woods 1999).

Manisa-Turkey.name: Manisa
Manisa-Turkey.evidence_basis: Imperial treasury and mint of the Nicaean Laskaris emperors (1222-1261), then capital of the Sarukhanid Beylik (1313) and major 15th-c. Ottoman sehzade residence (Emecen 1989; Foss).

Jerusalem-Palestine.name: Jerusalem
Jerusalem-Palestine.evidence_basis: Historic 90 ha walled footprint depopulated by the 1099 Crusader massacre, repopulated to ~28k-30k under Latin kings (Prawer; Boas), disrupted by 1244 Khwarazmian sack, revived under Mamluk waqf patronage (Burgoyne) before plague and 15th-c. contraction.

Famagusta-Cyprus.name: Famagusta
Famagusta-Cyprus.evidence_basis: Modest coastal town that boomed after 1291 with refugees and Italian merchants from fallen Acre into a premier Levantine entrepot (~100 ha walled area); devastated by 1348 plague and steep decline after 1373 Genoese seizure (Edbury; Coureas; Jacoby).

Kastamonu-Turkey.name: Kastamonu
Kastamonu-Turkey.evidence_basis: Capital of the Chobanid and Candarid (Isfendiyarid) Beyliks supported by Kure copper mines; Ibn Battuta in c. 1332 called it one of the largest and finest cities in Rum (Cahen; Yucel 1980).

Jeddah-Saudi Arabia.name: Jeddah
Jeddah-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Modest pilgrimage harbor for Mecca (Ibn Jubayr 1183) that expanded dramatically after Mamluk Sultan Barsbay redirected Indian Ocean spice fleets directly from Aden to Jeddah in the 1420s-30s (Meloy 2010; Vallet).

Aksaray-Turkey.name: Aksaray
Aksaray-Turkey.evidence_basis: Refounded and colonized with merchants and artisans by Qilij Arslan II in the 1170s as a royal Seljuk military-caravan hub; described by Ibn Battuta in the 1330s with active markets and akhi lodges (Peacock 2021; Oral 1962).

Kish-Iran.name: Kish
Kish-Iran.evidence_basis: Harireh archaeological city (~120 ha) dominated Persian Gulf maritime and pearl trade after Siraf's decline (Benjamin of Tudela; Yaqut; Kauz) until conquered and eclipsed by Island Hormuz in 1330.

Qalhat-Oman.name: Qalhat
Qalhat-Oman.evidence_basis: Excavated 35 ha walled coastal emporium with Bibi Maryam mosque and hammam (Rougeulle 2010, 2017); served as Omani twin capital of the Kingdom of Hormuz exporting Arabian horses to India (Marco Polo; Ibn Battuta) prior to 1508 Portuguese sack.

Gaza-Palestine.name: Gaza
Gaza-Palestine.evidence_basis: Elevated to a major Mamluk provincial capital (niyaba) under Governor Sanjar al-Jawli (1311-20) as the strategic caravan and postal gate between Cairo and Syria; praised as populous by Ibn Battuta (Lapidus; Sharon).

Dvin-Armenia.name: Dvin
Dvin-Armenia.evidence_basis: Shaddadid and Georgian-Mkhargrdzeli administrative center in the Ararat plain (Guven 2024; Hewsen 2001), devastated in 1236 by Chormaqan's Mongols and eclipsed by Yerevan as a small village by the 15th century.

Sari-Iran.name: Sari
Sari-Iran.evidence_basis: Bavandid royal seat and later Marashi Sayyid capital in eastern Mazandaran; damaged in 1221 and Timur's 1392 campaign before 15th-c. silk-agriculture recovery (Marashi; Mustawfi).

Malatya-Turkey.name: Malatya
Malatya-Turkey.evidence_basis: Old Malatya walled perimeter (~70 ha) thrived as a multi-confessional Syriac-Armenian-Muslim frontier city under Danishmendids and Rum Seljuks before 1315 Mamluk sack and border instability (Cahen; Michael the Syrian).

Tyre-Lebanon.name: Tyre
Tyre-Lebanon.evidence_basis: Fortified peninsular port (~40 ha) famous for glass, sugar and silk under Fatimids and Venetians/Crusaders (Ibn Jubayr; Prawer); systematically dismantled by Mamluks in 1291 to prevent Frankish return.

Karaman-Turkey.name: Karaman
Karaman-Turkey.evidence_basis: Primary seat of the Karamanid Beylik from the late 13th century with major madrasa and imaret endowments, tapering slightly after Ottoman annexation in 1468 (Cahen; Sumer).

Homs-Syria.name: Homs
Homs-Syria.evidence_basis: Walled Orontes plain city and Ayyubid/Mamluk military staging ground (three major Mamluk-Ilkhanid battles 1260-1299); modest commercial recovery in late Mamluk period (Ibn Battuta; Lapidus).

Sohar-Oman.name: Sohar
Sohar-Oman.evidence_basis: Former early Islamic Indian Ocean metropolis (~75 ha excavated core; Kervran 2004) that declined steadily after Buyid-Kerman conflicts and the rise of Kish, Hormuz and Qalhat (al-Idrisi; Ibn al-Mujawir).

Lar-Iran.name: Lar
Lar-Iran.evidence_basis: Seat of the local Miladi/Gorgin-Milad rulers of Larestan; rose rapidly in the 14th-15th centuries as the principal inland caravan staging hub and silver larin minting center between Shiraz and Hormuz (Aubin 1969).

Baku-Azerbaijan.name: Baku
Baku-Azerbaijan.evidence_basis: Walled Icheri Sheher (~22 ha) plus harbor suburbs grew after the 1192 Shamakhi earthquake as the Shirvanshahs' secondary capital, naphtha/silk port and 15th-c. royal palace complex (Minorsky 1958; Ashurbeyli).

Rasht-Iran.name: Rasht
Rasht-Iran.evidence_basis: Rose from a minor Biya-Pas settlement (noted by Mustawfi 1340) into Gilan's expanding raw-silk commercial center as Caspian silk exports to Tabriz and Genoa surged in the 14th-15th centuries (Goto; Rabino).

Van-Turkey.name: Van
Van-Turkey.evidence_basis: Fortified rock citadel and walled lower town on Lake Van (Vaspurakan -> Byzantine -> Seljuk -> Qara Qoyunlu stronghold), described by Mustawfi and surviving Timur's 1387 siege (Sinclair; Hewsen 2001).

Izmir-Turkey.name: Izmir
Izmir-Turkey.evidence_basis: Nicaean naval base and Aydinid/Hospitaller divided port (Upper Kadifekale and Harbor Castle); severely damaged by 1344 Crusade, Black Death and Timur's 1402 storming before Ottoman recovery (Vryonis; Zachariadou).

Sinope-Turkey.name: Sinope
Sinope-Turkey.evidence_basis: Conquered by Kaykaus I in 1214 (Ibn Bibi; Peacock 2021) as Seljuk Black Sea naval arsenal and Crimean trade link; later Candarid port with Genoese factory before 1461 Ottoman annexation (Cahen).

Yerevan-Armenia.name: Yerevan
Yerevan-Armenia.evidence_basis: Gradually superseded ruined Dvin and Ani as the administrative and commercial center of the Ararat plain (Chukhur-i Saad) during Ilkhanid, Timurid and Qara/Aq Qoyunlu rule (Hewsen 2001).

Hasankeyf-Turkey.name: Hasankeyf
Hasankeyf-Turkey.evidence_basis: Artuqid capital (great Tigris stone bridge c. 1116) and Ayyubid principality (1232-1462) controlling the upper Tigris crossing until annexed by the Aq Qoyunlu (Gabriel 1940; Sinclair).

Kunduz-Afghanistan.name: Kunduz
Kunduz-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Irrigated Tokharistan oasis hub (early medieval Walwalij) devastated in 1221, later fortified and revived as a key Timurid and Badakhshan-frontier garrison seat (Ibn Battuta; Baburnama).

Qatif-Saudi Arabia.name: Qatif
Qatif-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Coastal date-oasis and Gulf pearling port praised as a large fine town with extensive palm groves by Ibn Battuta (1331), serving Uyunid, Hormuzi and Jabrid maritime trade (Aubin; Potter).

Kars-Turkey.name: Kars
Kars-Turkey.evidence_basis: Bagratid kingdom seat until 1064, captured by Georgia in 1206 and later residence of Atabeg Sadun Mankaberdeli (Kartlis Tskhovreba; Guven 2024); raided by Timur in 1386 and contested by Qara Qoyunlu.

Zafar-Oman.name: Zafar
Zafar-Oman.evidence_basis: Excavated 64 ha walled port city of Al-Balid (Jansen; Costa) thriving as the Habudhi and Rasulid frankincense and war-horse export hub to India (Marco Polo; Ibn Battuta; Vallet).

Manama-Bahrain.name: Manama
Manama-Bahrain.evidence_basis: Excavated medieval capital of Awal/Bahrain Island at Bilad al-Qadim (Al-Khamis Mosque; Insoll 2005) and adjacent harbor quarter, prospering on Gulf pearl fisheries under Uyunid, Hormuzi and Jabrid rule.

Alanya-Turkey.name: Alanya
Alanya-Turkey.evidence_basis: Refounded and heavily fortified by Ala al-Din Kayqubad I in 1221 with Red Tower, arsenal and 6.5 km citadel walls as Seljuk winter capital and timber-export port to Mamluk Egypt (Redford 2000; Ibn Battuta).

Muscat-Oman.name: Muscat
Muscat-Oman.evidence_basis: Sheltered rocky harbor under Hormuzi vassalage that grew steadily in the 14th-15th centuries as a provisioning and date-export port supplementing Qalhat (al-Idrisi; Ibn Majid; Aubin).

Afyonkarahisar-Turkey.name: Afyonkarahisar
Afyonkarahisar-Turkey.evidence_basis: Seljuk treasury fortress and Sahipataoglu Beylik capital controlling the central-western Anatolian road junction and opium-trade hinterland (Cahen; Faroqhi).

Sinjar-Iraq.name: Sinjar
Sinjar-Iraq.evidence_basis: Zengid and Ayyubid sub-capital famed for irrigated orchards and bathhouses (Ibn Jubayr; Yaqut); sacked by Mongols in 1262 alongside Mosul and reduced to a secondary Jazira town (Mustawfi).

Barda-Azerbaijan.name: Barda
Barda-Azerbaijan.evidence_basis: Oxford AEB excavations (Campbell 2021; Wordsworth 2018) show that despite Yaqut's dismissal, Barda revived in the late 12th c., maintained craft/mint continuity under Ilkhanid patronage (1322 tomb tower), and declined after Ilkhanid collapse.

Najaf-Iraq.name: Najaf
Najaf-Iraq.evidence_basis: Pilgrimage city surrounding the Shrine of Imam Ali that steadily absorbed population from declining nearby Kufa, endowed with Ilkhanid and Jalayirid canals and hospices (Ibn Battuta 1327; Mustawfi).

Bam-Iran.name: Bam
Bam-Iran.evidence_basis: Walled mudbrick citadel and town (Arg-e Bam ~18 ha core plus qanat-fed palm/cotton suburbs) on the Kerman-Sistan highway noted by al-Muqaddasi, Yaqut and Mustawfi (1340) for fine cotton textiles.

Al-Shihr-Yemen.name: Al-Shihr
Al-Shihr-Yemen.evidence_basis: Principal medieval port of Hadramawt replacing Sharma (c. 1150; Rougeulle 2015); exported frankincense, horses and fish under Rasulid and Kathiri suzerainty (Vallet 2010).

Niksar-Turkey.name: Niksar
Niksar-Turkey.evidence_basis: Early capital of the Danishmendid dynasty (Yagibasan Madrasa, 1157) with fortified citadel (~25 ha), later a secondary Seljuk and Tajeddinoglu provincial town in the Kelkit valley (Cahen).

Samsun-Turkey.name: Samsun
Samsun-Turkey.evidence_basis: Twin Black Sea emporium of Muslim Samsun and Genoese Simisso serving as the northern maritime outlet of Sivas until burnt during early 15th-c. Ottoman-Candarid consolidation (Bryer; Cahen).

Beirut-Lebanon.name: Beirut
Beirut-Lebanon.evidence_basis: Ibelin Crusader lordship and pine-timber port; unlike Acre and Tyre, retained as the chief Mamluk maritime outlet for Damascus spice exports to Venice and Genoa in the 14th-15th centuries (Ashtor; Fuess).

Tikrit-Iraq.name: Tikrit
Tikrit-Iraq.evidence_basis: Fortified Tigris bluff town and major Syriac Orthodox maphrianate center until destroyed and depopulated during Timur's 1393 siege (Yaqut; Ibn Arabshah).

Tehran-Iran.name: Tehran
Tehran-Iran.evidence_basis: Orchard suburb of Rayy described by Yaqut (c. 1220) as twelve subterranean-house districts; steadily absorbed displaced Rayy inhabitants and was noted as a sizable unwalled town by Clavijo in 1404 (Mustawfi; Rante 2015).

Nizwa-Oman.name: Nizwa
Nizwa-Oman.evidence_basis: Falaj-irrigated interior oasis capital of the Omani Imamate and Nabhanid kings (1154-1470), documented by Ibn Battuta and Omani chronicles as the principal inland urban center (Wilkinson 1987).

Safad-Israel.name: Safad
Safad-Israel.evidence_basis: Templar fortress rebuilt after 1266 by Baybars as the Mamluk provincial capital of Galilee, absorbing inland urban populations after the 1291 destruction of coastal Acre and Tyre and Sephardic arrivals after 1492 (al-Dimashqi; Lapidus).

Farah-Afghanistan.name: Farah
Farah-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Walled fortress-oasis on the Farah Rud linking Herat and Zaranj; prospered under Kartids and Timurids after absorbing trade displaced from ruined Zaranj after 1383 (Hafiz-i Abru; Ball).

Tarim-Yemen.name: Tarim
Tarim-Yemen.evidence_basis: Inland Wadi Hadramawt scholarly and mudbrick-palace oasis ruled by Banu Yamani and Ba Alawi sayyids, sustained by flash-flood spate agriculture and Red Sea-Indian Ocean remittances (Serjeant; Boxberger).

Nablus-Palestine.name: Nablus
Nablus-Palestine.evidence_basis: Rich agricultural, olive-oil and soap-manufacturing center of central Palestine attested by Yaqut, Ibn Battuta and Crusader/Mamluk fiscal surveys (Ellenblum; Ashtor).

Maimana-Afghanistan.name: Maimana
Maimana-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Farighunid and Seljuk market town of Juzjan on the Herat-Balkh piedmont highway; disrupted by 1221 Mongol campaign before recovering under Kartid and Timurid rule (Hudud al-Alam; Hafiz-i Abru).

Latakia-Syria.name: Latakia
Latakia-Syria.evidence_basis: Northern Syrian harbor contested by Byzantines, Crusaders and Ayyubids, retaining active Mamluk-Cypriot and Genoese cotton/timber trade after Qalawun's 1287 takeover (Ashtor).

Karbala-Iraq.name: Karbala
Karbala-Iraq.evidence_basis: Walled Shi'i sanctuary and palm-grove oasis sustained by Euphrates canals (Nahr al-Husayniyya) and Jalayirid patronage; described by Ibn Battuta and Mustawfi as a flourishing shrine town.

Karak-Jordan.name: Karak
Karak-Jordan.evidence_basis: Fortified in 1142 by Pagan the Butler as Crusader Oultrejordain hub, becoming an Ayyubid principality and Mamluk imperial treasury/niyaba capital (Milwright 2008).

Sheki-Azerbaijan.name: Sheki
Sheki-Azerbaijan.evidence_basis: Foothill silk-weaving and commercial town linking Kakheti and Shirvan, ruled as a semi-autonomous principality (Orlat/Qara Qoyunlu vassal) in the late 14th-15th centuries (Minorsky; Mustawfi).

Sidon-Lebanon.name: Sidon
Sidon-Lebanon.evidence_basis: Walled coastal town and Crusader lordship (battlefield mass graves excavated by Mikulski 2019); razed in 1291 and modestly rebuilt as a secondary Mamluk port for the Biqaa and Damascus hinterland.

Hebron-Palestine.name: Hebron
Hebron-Palestine.evidence_basis: Pilgrimage town around the Ibrahimi Mosque expanded under Mamluk patronage (al-Jawli mosque, glassworks, waqf soup kitchens) as noted by Ibn Battuta and Mujir al-Din (Sharon).

Limassol-Cyprus.name: Limassol
Limassol-Cyprus.evidence_basis: Primary southern Lusignan harbor and sugar-estate export point (Kolossi/Episkopi); eclipsed commercially by Famagusta after 1291 and severely raided by Genoese (1373) and Mamluks (1425-26) (Edbury; Coureas).

Larnaca-Cyprus.name: Larnaca
Larnaca-Cyprus.evidence_basis: Known as Salines for its royal salt-lake exports; expanded markedly after the 1373 Genoese capture of Famagusta made it the Lusignan kingdom's main royal port and Venetian commercial hub (Coureas; Arbel).

Quba-Azerbaijan.name: Quba
Quba-Azerbaijan.evidence_basis: Northern Shirvan market and fortress town controlling the piedmont corridor toward Derbent and the Caspian littoral trade (Minorsky 1958; Yaqut).

Salt-Jordan.name: Salt
Salt-Jordan.evidence_basis: Replaced declining Amman as chief administrative fortress of the Balqa under Ayyubid al-Muazzam Isa (citadel 1220) and Mamluk Sultan Baybars (Walker 2011; Abu al-Fida).

Paphos-Cyprus.name: Paphos
Paphos-Cyprus.evidence_basis: Western Byzantine and Lusignan bishopric and sugar-producing district (Kouklia); harbor silted and castle ruined by the 1222 earthquake, shifting settlement uphill to Ktima (von Wartburg; Edbury).

Kyrenia-Cyprus.name: Kyrenia
Kyrenia-Cyprus.evidence_basis: Compact fortified northern Lusignan harbor and royal stronghold linking Cyprus to Cilician Armenia and southern Anatolia, heavily reinforced under Lusignan and Venetian rule (Edbury).
